video.title: How to Build & Sell Micro Apps in 2026 (Using Only AI)

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates building a niche CRM micro-app for independent pool service operators using only AI, with no coding. He uses Claude to pick a growing niche, then compares Claude Code, Replit and ChatGPT on the same prompt: Claude Code built it in about 2 minutes and was best, Replit took about 16 minutes, ChatGPT was fast but gave code without a preview. He then runs a back-of-envelope market sizing (79,000 US pool businesses, 1,000 customers at $20-$100/month) and outlines customer-finding methods: Facebook groups for feedback, Gummy Search for Reddit pain points, Claude deep research, Google Trends, scraping and cold outreach, and Facebook custom-audience ads. Key takeaway: niche vertical SaaS is cheap to prototype with AI, and validation and distribution are the real work.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Niche CRM for pool service operators
ideas.one_liner: AI-built, dead-simple vertical CRM sold by monthly subscription to independent pool service businesses.
ideas.customer: Independent, solo or small pool service operators (about 79,000 businesses in the US per Google, fragmented market)
ideas.problem: Generic CRMs like HubSpot are too expensive and complex for most small business owners and do not feel built for the pool industry.
ideas.offer: Simple web app with pool-specific fields (pool type, gallons, service day, frequency, gate code, rate per visit, equipment, notes), a day-of-week to-do filter, status colours and revenue dashboards (active pools, weekly revenue, monthly projected).

pricing.notes: Hypothetical only; no real customers or prices tested. Stripe integration planned but not built.

acquisition_channels.details: Join private, well-moderated, active pool-professional Facebook groups (e.g. Texas Pool Pros), ask what the perfect CRM would do, then DM contributors at launch offering free use in exchange for feedback, reviews, referrals and case studies. Prefer smaller moderated groups over large spammy ones.

quote.text: you can go back to all the people that commented or liked or helped you out and DM them and say, "Hey, thank you for helping me. Would you like to use this for free?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Scrape pool service businesses with Outscraper, then email, text or call offering free software for 90 days or free until the first five customers, converting to paid later.

quote.text: Use something like outscraper to scrape every single pool service business in your area.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Upload scraped list of all 79,000 businesses as a Facebook custom audience so ads show only to pool service owners; use pain points from research in ad copy to lower acquisition cost.
Research pain points via Gummy Search (Reddit aggregation) and Claude deep research to shape the product and messaging; Google Trends shows 'pool service software' searches spiking in 2025.

ideas.delivery: Software delivered as a web app built by Claude Code (no human coding); iterated with follow-up prompts (e.g. making records editable). Hosting, Stripe billing and deployment not shown.
unit_economics_claims: 1,000 customers at $20/month = $20,000/month (about 1.5% of 79,000 US pool businesses)
1,000 customers at $100/month = $100,000/month, with lower conversion at higher price
Claude Code build took under 2 minutes plus about 2 minutes for one follow-up prompt
ideas.startup_cost: not stated (AI tool subscriptions only implied)

acquisition.how: Facebook group engagement and DMs are manual; scraped cold outreach to sole traders (many pool operators) is restricted by UK PECR for email/SMS, and calls need TPS screening. Facebook custom-audience ads and SEO are automatable.

onboarding.how: Self-serve signup with in-app empty-state guidance can be largely unattended; Stripe checkout is standard.

delivery.how: Software product; agents can build and maintain features, with occasional human review of releases and hosting.

support.how: AI chat support and docs can handle most queries; bugs and data issues need occasional human approval.

uk_applicability.notes: Software and pricing work the same. UK pool service market is much smaller than the US and pool numbers/climate are less favourable, so the niche should be re-sized or swapped (e.g. other UK trades). UK GDPR and PECR limit cold email/SMS to sole traders; limited companies are fine.

risks: Market size and 'growing fast' claims are unvalidated; the host admits he does not know the pool industry
No customers, retention or willingness to pay tested
Incumbent field-service software already exists in the niche
Scraped outreach may breach PECR/GDPR in the UK
AI-generated code may have security, data and reliability gaps for paid customers

tactics.name: Use AI to pick a rising, fragmented niche
steps: Prompt Claude for 10 niches in local/home services growing fast, backed by hard data
Reject niches likely to be concentrated among a few big firms
Prefer industries with many solo operators
Pick one and sanity-check with Google Trends

quote.text: I want an industry that's highly fragmented with a lot of solo operators.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Prompt-build a niche MVP and compare tools
steps: Write one prompt: dead simple, niche-specific, fewer fields than generic CRMs, 'I have no coding experience, show me the UI'
Paste the same prompt into Claude Code, Replit and ChatGPT and time each
Ask for fixes by follow-up prompt (e.g. make records editable)
Tell each tool the others are competing to push quality

quote.text: You always want to make the apps jealous of each other or competitive with each other.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Validate and seed customers via Facebook groups
steps: Search 'pool service' in Facebook groups and filter by near me
Favour private, moderated, active groups; skip big spammy ones and groups with no posts
Join and ask what the perfect CRM would do, then implement the feedback
At launch DM helpers offering free use in return for feedback, reviews, referrals and case studies

quote.text: oftentimes smaller is better because it's easier for the managers to wrap their arms around it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Mine pain points with Gummy Search and deep research
steps: Use Gummy Search to pull Reddit pain points and desired features
Run Claude deep research on what operators hate, love and cannot live without in current software
Feed findings into product features and ad copy to cut acquisition cost

tactics.name: Scrape and target the full niche list
steps: Scrape all pool service businesses with Outscraper
Offer 90 days free or free until first five customers
Upload the list to Facebook Ads as a custom audience to show ads only to those owners

lessons.lesson: Pick niches that are growing and fragmented with many solo operators, not concentrated or shrinking ones.
AI coding tools differ greatly in speed and non-coder friendliness; test the same prompt across several and choose by preview quality and iteration speed.
A conservative price plus small market share gives a simple revenue model, but this math is hypothetical until conversion is proven.
Co-design with community members and give early users free access in exchange for reviews, referrals and case studies.
Use AI research and Reddit mining to find pain points before building and reuse them in ad messaging.
Domain-specific defaults (pool type, gate code, service day) make software feel purpose-built versus generic CRMs.
The build is now the cheap part; distribution and getting paying customers is the real work.

evidence_quality.rationale: Live demo of AI tools is genuine first-hand, but the business is hypothetical: no customers, revenue or validated demand, and market math is illustrative. Growth claims come from AI output.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Description links to Claude Code (likely affiliate/sponsor); host also promotes his own Facebook ads video.
